title: backgroundColor for datatable (DT) not working for grid_page
description:
I have a shiny app built with a grid_page.
There is a datatable (DT) output
I do some formatting on the datatable. Most of the formatting works (hover, stripes, fontsize, etc....)

However, background color does not work.

Reproducible example follows:

```
library(shiny)
library(plotly)
library(gridlayout)
library(bslib)
library(DT)
library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(
  x = c(-.5, -.1, 0, .1, .5),
  y = c("Dark Red", "Light Red", "White", "Light Green", "Dark Green")
)

formatdetails <- function(x){
  x <- 
    x %>% 
    datatable(
      rownames = FALSE,
      class = list(stripe = FALSE),
      options = list(
        pageLength = 5,
        lengthMenu = c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25),
        order = list(1, 'asc')
      )
    ) %>% 
    formatStyle(
      columns = "x",
      target = "row",
      backgroundColor = styleInterval(
        cuts = c(-.2, -.05, .05, .2),
        values = rev(c("#005600", "#42A644", "#F1F1F1", "#DD6BA6", "#841859"))
      ),
      color = styleInterval(
        cuts = c(-.2, -.05, .05, .2),
        values = c("#e6e6e6", "#e6e6e6", "#0d0d0d", "#e6e6e6", "#e6e6e6")
      )
    )  %>% 
    formatStyle(columns = c(1:4), fontSize = '80%')
} 

ui <- grid_page(
  layout = c(
    "header header",
    "area2  .     "
  ),
  row_sizes = c(
    "100px",
    "1fr"
  ),
  col_sizes = c(
    "590px",
    "1fr"
  ),
  gap_size = "1rem",
  grid_card_text(
    area = "header",
    content = "Test",
    alignment = "start",
    is_title = FALSE
  ),
  grid_card(
    area = "area2",
    card_body(DTOutput(outputId = "tblcard", width = "100%"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
   
output$tblcard <- renderDT(df %>% formatdetails())

}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
  
The resulting table is all white:

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/gridlayout/assets/25011558/f0dba0cf-0700-461b-aa83-9e5911f7b81c)

title: Automatic number of columns
description:
I stumbled across this example of having automatic number of columns depending on the width of the window [here](https://css-tricks.com/books/greatest-css-tricks/flexible-grids/)

Is something like this possible with gridlayout in R?

title: Reactive grid sizing
description:
Is it possible to make the row heights of grid elements respond to reactive variables?

Imagine we have a simple app with a select box and a plot, we might declare the grid layout like this:

```r
grid_config <- new_gridlayout(
  c( 
      "1rem  1fr",
      "150px select_box",
      "400px plot"
   )
)
```
Now, let's assume we want to change the height of `plot` (currently set at 400px), depending upon the input of `select_box`. I've tried setting the heights to `auto`, but for my particular use case, the plots are not printed adequately and require fine tuning by specifying the pixels depending upon the input of a select box. Is there any method to do this fine tuning?

I thought that a new reactive variable that tracks the input into `select_box` and creates row heights could be created, and inserted into the above vector. But, this wouldn't work as `new_gridlayout()` isn't reactive and is instead a UI function to generate HTML (if I am not mistaken).

title: Changing `grid_card` collapsible behaviour
description:
When a `grid_card()` is made collapsible, I think the default behaviour doesn't match what one may expect. Specifically, I would expect the card to act like a standard accordion (e.g., like the [Bootstrap v5.0 accordion](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.0/components/accordion/)) in that:

- The card/accordion is collapsed by default if `collapsible = true` (i.e.,  it can be expanded only if a user wants to discover more information)
- Any part of the the title of the card can be clicked to expand/collapse the card, not just the small arrow symbol as is currently implemented

I just wanted to pass on the feedback in case useful, as personally I would benefit from the default behaviour changing. Thanks!

title: Add 'alignment' arg to all content containers
description:
Currently, only `grid_card_text()` has an  `alignment` argument to allow the alignment of text within the card. Given all text in a `grid_card_text()` gets wrapped in a `h3` tag (or custom tag you set in the `wrapping_tag` argument), I prefer to pass blocks of text (e.g., a title and a paragraph) into a single `grid_card()` call like so:

```r
grid_card(
  area = "intro_text",
  tags$h4("My title"),
  tags$p("My paragraph of text"),
  class = "intro_text"
)
```

I find doing this allows for the easy grouping of different types of text (e.g., titles and paragraphs) into a single card. The only way I have found to left-align the text in this instance is to override the default alignment of all content containers by setting the following attribute in my global CSS file:

```CSS
.grid_card.vertical_stack .panel-content{
  align-items: start;
}
```

I've tried setting `align-items` for a specific `grid_card` by using custom classes (e.g., for my example `grid_card()` above):

```CSS
.intro_text .grid_card.vertical_stack .panel-content{
  align-items: start;
}
```
But this fails to change anything. I suspect I am running into a CSS inheritance issue when doing this, but I have not yet been able to work this out.

This led me to wonder, would it be possible to have an `aligment` argument to all types of content containers (e.g., `grid_card()`) to allow a card-by-card selection of how the content is aligned? This might prove useful outside of aligning text in my specific example.

Thanks as ever for the great package.

title: Arguments not being passed to `grid_card`
description:
The `grid_card_text()` function does not appear to be passing on arguments to `grid_card()` using the ellipsis. For example setting `has_border = FALSE` in `grid_card_text()` does not remove the border from the card. Reprex below:

```r
library(shiny)
library(gridlayout)

ui <- grid_page(
  layout = c(
    "    1fr   ",
    "1fr header"
  ),
  grid_card_text("header", "Test header", has_border = FALSE)
)

server <- function(input, output) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
I'm not sure if this is my user error or an error with the function. Any help would be appreciated.

title: Unable to install gridlayout inside an `{renv}` project
description:
I wanted to try out `{gridlayout}` and `{shinyuieditor}` inside a project with the packages managed by [`{renv}`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/index.html) . However this is the first time I've encountered the following error regarding a missing `package.rds` file:

```
> renv::install("rstudio/gridlayout")
Retrieving 'https://api.github.com/repos/rstudio/gridlayout/tarball/37b68b2c0989912c7d40226dd15d3be50039fb2f' ...
	OK [downloaded 4.7 Mb in 0.7 secs]
Installing magrittr [2.0.3] ...
	OK [linked cache]
Installing digest [0.6.29] ...
	OK [linked cache]
Installing base64enc [0.1-3] ...
	OK [linked cache]
Installing rlang [1.0.4] ...
	OK [linked cache]
Installing fastmap [1.1.0] ...
	OK [linked cache]
Installing htmltools [0.5.3] ...
	OK [linked cache]
Installing gridlayout [0.1.0] ...
	FAILED
Error in gzfile(file, "rb") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In gzfile(file, "rb") :
  cannot open compressed file '/home/eric/r_dev_projects/silly_test/renv/staging/1/gridlayout/Meta/package.rds', probable reason 'No such file or directory'
```

I'm not familiar with the `Meta` directory within an R package structure (I checked out the second edition of [R Packages](https://r-pkgs.org/) and didn't see a mention of it). To ensure this wasn't an `{renv}` problem installing remote packages from GitHub, I was able to install [`{connectapi}`](https://github.com/rstudio/connectapi)  via `renv::install("rstudio/connectapi")` with no issues at all.  Happy to provide more diagnostics if it helps/

title: use of animate parameter in shiny sliderinput not accepted
description:
I don't know if this is a gridlayout issue but the same element parameters work in a non-gridlayout version of the shiny app.
The shiny ui editor does not provide the ability to add the `animate` parameter to `sliderInput` so I added it manually.  This code works in the original app:

```
 sliderInput("point","Number of points drawn",min=2,max=points,value=2,step=5,
                  animate=animationOptions(interval=points/60*2))
```
This code using gridlayout triggers a "non-numeric argument to binary operator" error.

```
  gridlayout::grid_panel_stack(
    area = "sidebar",
    item_alignment = "top",
    item_gap = "12px",
    shiny::sliderInput(
      inputId = "point",
      label = "Points Drawn",
      min = 1L,
      max = 6000L,
      value = 1L,
      animate=animationOptions(interval=points/60*2)
    ),

```
After I change the animate parameter simply to TRUE the app runs but ignores it.
```
  gridlayout::grid_panel_stack(
    area = "sidebar",
    item_alignment = "top",
    item_gap = "12px",
    shiny::sliderInput(
      inputId = "point",
      label = "Points Drawn",
      min = 1L,
      max = 6000L,
      value = 1L,
      animate=TRUE
    ),

```

Full code here: https://github.com/apsteinmetz/sve_beta_spiro.git

title: grid_panel overflow should be auto
description:
With `overflow: scroll`, the scroll bars are always shown, even if they're not actually needed for the content. (On my Mac, I also have "Show scroll bars" set to Always.)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/86978/118757941-a79f2600-b833-11eb-917c-50f730feaa25.png)

With `overflow: auto`, the scroll bars will appear only when needed.

title: Ability to dynamically move panel to different place in grid
description:
Would be useful to have something allowing a given panel to be shuffled. 

Two ways I see this working:

1. A whole new layout
```r
# server.r
gridlayout::update_layout(new_layout)
```

2. Just moving a single panel
```r
# server.r
gridlayout::move_panel("panel_id", start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col)
```

Would require injecting some javascript to handle move requests.
